rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Sequential pronoun/demonstrative check across all chunks: line 9 'You're new to this country: the stretch where the agent runs alone and you don't watch each step. Don't travel it like a tourist.' -- the appositive after the colon defines 'this country' in the same sentence, so 'it' resolves in-chunk. 'the result'/'that' (ch.1) resolve to the immediately preceding sentence. 'the return' (ch.2, 'after you've read the return') is arc-earned spine vocabulary, independently grounded in the enclosing module's own prior context (run-the-first-experiment.md line 57 'will surface on the return' and its 'Reading the return' lecture link, both preceding this lecture in module include order). 'it'/'the thin spots'/'the agent' (ch.3) are named earlier in the same chunk. 'it' in 'stop it' / 'letting it run' (ch.4) refers to the run/agent established from chunk 1's apparatus framing, reused per the same-file-term carve-out. No unresolved referent remains.

First sentence/bullet of each chunk checked for positional callbacks: ch.1 'You are testing, and you are learning' (none), ch.2 'Same task, two runs' (none), ch.3 '**Gap analysis**: walk the system you have against the system the task needs' (none), ch.4 'Cancel is legitimate; traces are data' (restates own header, none). No 'the opening lecture said' style phrasing, and no other file named or implied by position anywhere in the body.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Every backward reference points at a beat that exists.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No 'the X you did/saw/caught' backward-beat construction appears in the body. 'a specific gap you just saw' (ch.2, line 14) narrates the generic run-two pattern hypothetically, part of the two-run-arc explanation, not a literal callback to a completed module beat, so there is no dead-beat risk to check against the module's exercise set.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Live-demo beats survive a text read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No guess-before-reveal / predict-then-watch instruction appears anywhere in the body.
Every chunk (1-4) carries a multi-sentence or multi-bullet self-standing claim tied to its own header; none is a bare wait-state or single context-dependent bullet.

'Every send-off is an experiment' (ch.1), 'The two-run arc' (ch.2), 'Gap analysis: walk your system against the task' (ch.3), and 'Cancel is legitimate; traces are data' (ch.4, restated verbatim as the chunk's own first bullet) each accurately summarize their chunk's content; no header is contradicted by its body.

Checked all sub-items across all chunks: no 'Not X. Not Y. Z.' construction anywhere; no anaphora/epistrophe triples (ch.2's 'Run one... Run two...' is a two-item contrast, not a repeated-opener triple); no self-grading superlatives / value-prop leak; no number-with-own-retraction ('twenty minutes' and 'fifteen to thirty minutes' in ch.4 are stated plainly, never hedged then walked back); no abstraction-noun stacks (vocabulary stays concrete: agent, apparatus, rules, context, result, data, plan.md, verifier, reference artifact, thin spots); no empty-leg verb triplets -- ch.2's 'find what went wrong, watch each packaging piece close a specific gap, and send the same task again' and ch.4's 'hallucinating file paths, arguing with itself, or missing a requirement that wasn't in the prompt' are each three distinct, concrete items, not the stylized empty-leg pattern.
